children: shares climbed Monday despite another brief outage affecting Facebook and Instagram, suggesting investors are increasingly focused on the company's AI growth story rather than temporary disruptions across its core social-media platforms. The stock rose about 3% to roughly $683 in premarket trading as early adoption of Meta's new Muse AI agent added to optimism around returns on the company's enormous artificial-intelligence spending.

Downdetector recorded more than 17,000 Facebook outage reports and over 5,000 Instagram reports around 9:21 p.m. New York time Sunday. Reports dropped sharply within roughly two hours, limiting the apparent duration of the disruption.

Still, the outage adds to a recent pattern. Facebook and Instagram experienced another disruption in July, while more than 100,000 users were reportedly affected by problems across the platforms in June. Another significant outage occurred in March.
Investors largely looked through those issues Monday.

The bigger catalyst appears to be Muse, Meta's new personal AI agent, which recently reached the No. 1 position on Apple's U.S. App Store. Muse is designed to perform tasks on users' behalf, including opening apps, completing forms and sending emails, putting Meta more directly against OpenAI, Anthropic and Alphabet in the emerging consumer-agent market.

That matters because Meta has been spending aggressively on AI infrastructure, leaving investors increasingly focused on whether those investments can generate tangible engagement and revenue returns. Strong early adoption of Muse offers one of the clearest consumer-facing signals yet that Meta could translate its AI spending into products users actually seek out.

The outage itself is unlikely to change Meta's investment case unless service disruptions become longer or begin hurting engagement and advertising performance. The more important metrics are Muse user growth, retention and eventual monetization, along with evidence that AI is improving ad efficiency across Facebook and Instagram. Wall Street's average price target of roughly $759 implies additional upside from Monday's premarket level, but sustaining that optimism will require Meta to demonstrate that its huge AI spending is producing measurable revenue and engagement gains rather than simply higher capital costs.

title: Meta Platform Stock Sends Signal After Outage
